body_ar: (باب ما جاء في ذمة الله وذمة نبيه (ص) ): عقد هذا الباب لنوع آخر من التوحيد وهو الأدب مع الله سبحانه وتعالى، وذلك في ذمته بأن لا تعطى ذمته وذمة رسوله (ص) وإنما يعطي القائد ذمته وذمة من معه من المؤمنين إذا أراد عقد الذمة، والذمة العهد، وهي ما يذم بإخلافه، الذي إذا أخلفه الإنسان ذم به، فهذا الذي يسمى بالذمة، وذمة الله معناه عهده، وذمة نبيه (ص) معناه عهده، لقوله تعالى: {وأوفوا بعهد الله إذا عاهدتم}،
body_en: 'Chapter: what has come concerning the covenant of God and the covenant of His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace.' This chapter was set down for another kind of the oneness of God (tawḥīd), namely right conduct towards God, glorified and exalted — here, in the matter of His covenant (dhimmah): that God's covenant and the covenant of His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, are not to be granted. Rather, when a commander wishes to conclude a pledge of protection, he grants his own covenant and the covenant of those believers who are with him. The dhimmah is a pledge; it is that for the breaking of which one is blamed — that which, when a person breaks it, he is blamed for it. This is what is called the dhimmah. 'The covenant of God' means His pledge, and 'the covenant of His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace,' means his pledge — because of His words, exalted is He: {And fulfil the covenant of God when you have made a covenant} (Sūrat al-Naḥl 16:91),

The Sheikh's commentary series on Kitāb al-Tawḥīd
flags.note: Article 516 shows the series expounds Kitāb al-Tawḥīd of Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab, and article 508 quotes the base text in verse, so al-Mughnī al-Mufīd appears to be a versification (naẓm) of that book rather than a separate work by the Sheikh. The Sheikh's office should confirm the work and its author before the title is translated or expanded anywhere in the corpus; it has been left untranslated for now.

flags.context: وذلك في ذمته بأن لا تعطى ذمته وذمة رسوله (ص) وإنما يعطي القائد ذمته وذمة من معه من المؤمنين إذا أراد عقد الذمة
options: bond of protection (the dhimmah granted to a defeated enemy)
flags.note: The word carries two loads at once in this passage: the general sense of a binding pledge (which the Sheikh derives from ذم 'to blame') and the specific military sense of the safe-conduct a commander grants to an enemy on surrender. English has no single word covering both, and the etymological play on 'blame' is lost. 'Covenant' has been used for the general sense and 'pledge of protection' where the military act is meant; a reviewer should decide whether one word should be used throughout.

translator_notes: The published page carries only the opening excerpt of this lecture/sermon; the Arabic breaks off mid-sentence and the full text is offered on the site as a downloadable Word document. The English ends exactly where the Arabic ends. Nothing has been supplied to complete it.

This page belongs to the Sheikh's tape series on Kitāb al-Tawḥīd of Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab, identified in article 516, the first tape of the series. Passages in quotation marks are the base text being commented on; the unquoted text is the Sheikh's own commentary. The distinction is load-bearing and has been preserved.
Qur'anic renderings in this file are interpretive translations of meaning, offered to carry the Sheikh's argument in English. They are not a substitute for the Arabic text of the Qur'an.
The Sheikh's derivation الذمة ... ما يذم بإخلافه links dhimmah to dhamm, 'blame'. The English keeps the link explicit rather than dropping it, since the whole definition turns on it.
Despite the title 'the last tape', the page carries only the opening of the commentary on this chapter.
